speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Soon, many of us will be celebrating the Lunar New Year, another time for family gathering and feasting.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Have you booked a restaurant for the reunion dinner?

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: What new cookies and New Year goodies are there in the market?

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Where can we get fresh meat at good prices for our steamboat?

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I am sure these are plausibly some of the usual questions that are floating around at this time.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This year, I would like to invite Members to spare some thoughts on the safety and supply of these festive foods.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Often, in Singapore, we take our safe and secure food supply for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is the result of many decades of hard work by stakeholders and the trust that they have help built in the minds of the consumers.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Stakeholders, including Government agencies that have implemented relevant and effective policies, regularly reviewed and updated; businesses who have extended their supply network, instituted good food management practices and supported the growth of our food industry; and consumers who played an active role in ensuring food safety and supported our diversification policy and local food businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Over the decades, many agencies have been involved in the regulation and development of the food sector: the Primary Production Department, I am sure that sounds familiar to some of us here, was involved in regulating our local farming sector; the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority of Singapore (AVA) regulated food safety from importation, local production and manufacturing; the National Environment Agency (NEA) regulated food hygiene in the retail sector; the Health Sciences Authority supported food safety by rendering testing expertise to regulatory agencies; and Enterprise Singapore administered the Rice Stockpile Scheme to ensure adequate supplies of rice, mitigating the impact of any unforeseen disruptions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A new, single food Bill is essential as Singapore faces evolving new and rising food risks.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our global food supply network is expanding with our push for market diversification.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Consumers are demanding more and new types of foods.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Food safety hazards can arise at any point along the agri-food supply chain.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With advancements in science and technology, we have seen the emergence of new food production methods, inputs, such as pesticides, and novel food products.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore has also faced various food supply challenges in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic saw the impact of supply disruptions when we experienced the effects of lockdowns and restrictions on cross-border movements.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Supply chain disruptions arising from many other factors, extreme weather events, disease outbreaks and trade restrictions, also affected our food supply on several occasions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With climate change, rising biosecurity risks and geopolitical tensions, the risk of food disruptions is expected to increase.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our policy responses have helped us ride out these storms.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I will introduce the key legislative changes to the food safety regime.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon will elaborate on the details of the food safety regime and introduce the food security provisions under the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Minister of State for Health Rahayu Mahzam will elaborate on provisions related to health promotion.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill will become the main legislation that provides a regulatory framework covering food sector in Singapore, from farm to fork.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government recognises that a safe and secure food supply needs to be underpinned by streamlined regulations that facilitate compliance and business innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is not only vital for a healthy population and workforce, but also for a strong economy and continued local businesses' access to international markets.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This Bill will consolidate existing legislation in different Acts, standardise definitions across the industry, rationalise requirements across food types and establish common penalty frameworks.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This provides a common operating context, reduces complexity and, in turn, supports improved compliance with legal requirements directed at protecting public health.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I will elaborate on two elements in this aspect.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: One, the Bill will cover the distribution of food in all forms, whether through sale, movement of food items or given for free.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is an expansion of the current scope, which mainly covers sale.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This expansion of scope is important as food safety risks exist not just in the food that is sold.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Food that is given for free can also be unsafe and it is important to provide protection to recipients of donated food.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There may be some concerns among charities, food donors and entities which support their food distribution efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, these concerns have been addressed with the passing of the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act last year.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A food donor has legal immunity if the food donor can meet the four conditions in section 5 of Good Samaritan Food Donation Act.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Clause 164 in the Bill makes this clear.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: SFA has sought feedback from food charities and distribution groups on its guidelines for food donation and distribution.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The updated guidelines will be published later this month.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We hope these will provide more detailed guidance on safe food handling practices.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Two, current regulatory approaches are uneven across different groups of food industry participants and different food types.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Some of our legislation regulates by types of food, while others regulated by types of activities.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Part 3 of the Bill provides for a two-tier regulatory regime for trading of food-related commodities.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, for food imports, the first tier is the licensing of the food trader to ensure that they have the required systems and processes in the course of business to source safe and suitable food, ensure the integrity of items imported and to recall food if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The second tier is the requirement of a permit for every food consignment imported.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This second regulatory tool is necessary for food-specific safety requirements to be applied at the consignment level.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, when an animal disease outbreak excludes specific sources from supplying to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Today, most food traders are subjected to some form of a two-tier regime.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill will standardise and apply this two-tier approach to all kinds of food.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will ensure consistency across different food commodities and reduce regulatory complexity for food traders importing or exporting different food types.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: An exception is made by the Bill for the import of food for private consumption.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singaporeans often bring home food from overseas to enjoy them here or to share with friends and family.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill will set out the maximum quantity of food that individuals can bring in from overseas without the need for a licence and permit, provided none of the food is for use in the food business or for donation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This Bill calls this the private consumption exception.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Given such food is meant for consumption by the individual and family and not for wider distribution, the food safety risk to the public is significantly lower.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The private consumption exception will exclude food of higher regulatory concern, such as game meat or animal blood products.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The second thrust of the Bill is to strengthen our food safety regime to better protect consumers, support industry development and keep pace with emerging trends.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singaporeans rely a lot on food businesses for our daily meals – many of us either eat out or order food delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Strong regulation of food safety laws is therefore necessary to ensure public health and build public confidence in our food businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are strengthening our regulatory regime in two ways by: (a) providing for more comprehensive offences that apply along all steps of the food supply chain, regardless of commodity type and business activity; and (b) standardising the penalty frameworks including aligning maximum penalties.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Part 8 of the Bill will provide a common set of offences by rationalising the existing offences under the different Acts today.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, unlike the SOFA that makes selling unsafe or unsuitable food an offence, the current Wholesome Meat and Fish Act, or WMFA, covers meat and fish products only and not food in general; while the Environmental Public Health Act, or EPHA, covers only the retail setting.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Existing offences related to food handling processes are overly specific and prescriptive.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Yet, given the varied operating conditions of food businesses, it is ineffective for the law to specify every possible practice that might lead to unsafe food.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We cannot be constantly amending the law to deal with a new method of handling or production.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill outlines the offences in clauses 144, 145, 148 and 149.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This broader coverage seeks to ensure accountability of the food handlers who may come into contact with the food in the entire process.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It will also provide SFA with the flexibility to adapt to new food safety risks, as the industry evolves and new practices emerge.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will place greater emphasis on having good food control processes and afford better protection to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As part of rationalisation, some offences under existing laws are decriminalised.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is replaced with regulatory sanctions which are more immediate and effective in deterring unacceptable conduct by licensees.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Doing so will avoid criminalising persons for infringements that do not lead to direct harm or danger to people.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This change frees up the resources of the court system and enables SFA as a regulator to move faster by meting out regulatory sanctions directly.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For instance, where breaches in import licence conditions are administrative in nature, these will now no longer warrant prosecution in Court.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, SFA will still be able to take regulatory actions such as financial penalties and licence suspensions against such breaches.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Two, on standardising the penalty framework for offences, including aligning maximum penalties.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Currently, similar offences under the different Acts attract different penalties.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For instance, under the WMFA, an offender who sells meat or fish that is unfit for human consumption faces a maximum fine of $50,000, whereas he or she would face a fine of up to $5,000 under the SOFA if it was some other food.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This considers the existing penalties in the WMFA, which are the highest among existing food legislation and the Courts today have been meting out sentences close to the maximum fines for offences under the older food laws, which are much lower.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The actual quantum for each case remains to be a decision for the Courts to make on convicting the offender.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Further, current penalties may sometimes not commensurate with the severity of the impact from the offence committed or the culpability of the offenders as these offences had been enacted some time back.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill therefore organises the offences and their corresponding maximum penalties based on severity and threat to public health, culpability of offences and the circumstances of when, where and how the breach occurred.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, the more severe the offence, the higher the penalty.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A more severe breach, such as the supply of unsafe food will attract a higher criminal punishment than a less severe breach, such as failing to keep records.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There will also be differentiation between individuals and entities, and between first time offenders and repeat offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Part 14 of the Bill introduces a framework to disqualify certain persons from holding licences.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Today, all ex-licensees whose licences have been revoked, can reapply for the same licence immediately after conviction, even though they may still be unfit or unsuitable to carry on a food business.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Disqualification will only apply to ex-licensees who had their licences revoked.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Grounds of licence revocations include infringements that had posed severe risks to food safety or are in the public interest, non-compliance with Part 7 directions and fraud.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The actual disqualification period will be determined by SFA after considering factors, such as compliance history of the ex-licensee and the severity of the violation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The intent is to provide sufficient deterrence while avoiding being overly punitive.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The disqualification applies only to the activity or trade that the revocation of licence had covered.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Disqualified persons will not be allowed to be an executive staff in the same type of licensable food businesses at any premises, where they may be placed in charge of making decisions on the day-to-day operations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: By clause 347, a similar disqualification framework is introduced to Part 4 of the EPHA, in connection with licensing of temporary fair operators.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While operators of temporary fairs will continue to be licensed under the EPHA, food stalls in temporary fairs will be licensed under the Food Safety and Security Act when passed.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Introducing the disqualification framework in the EPHA ensures that the same treatment will apply to both temporary fair operators and food stall operators.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2017, special powers in the SOFA were conferred on the Director-General for Food Administration, or the DG (FA), to issue directions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This power has proven essential in securing immediate corrective actions or initiating recalls in the event of a food safety incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our priority is to protect consumers and to prevent or mitigate any serious danger to public health.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Part 7 of the Bill retains these powers.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will include directions to implement measures to prevent spread of diseases on farms, such as culling or movement control over animals.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There will also be a new direction in clause 130 aimed at the food worker lapses in a licensed food business environment.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Sometimes, the food safety lapse is due entirely to an individual, for example, failure of a food worker to maintain personal hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To manage contamination from food vending machines and equipment used in the food production process, directions may be issued under clause 124 to ensure cleanliness and production of safe and suitable food.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Such directions will be issued to the owner of a food vending machine or equipment.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Lastly, clause 134 extends directions on the maintenance of premises, equipment and dealing with source of contamination to animal feed production.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As with current day practice, the failure to comply with Part 7 directions constitute an offence.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: SFA works closely with other agencies as one Government, in the interest of protecting public health against food threats.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For instance, officers from the Ministry of Health (MOH) are appointed powers to enforce against non-compliances with nutrition and health claims.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Appointed officers from the Majlis Ugama Islam Singapore (MUIS) may also carry out monitoring and enforcement on halal labelling.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill will allow SFA to continue with the current practice, where SFA officers or officers of any other Singapore public sector agency may be appointed as food inspectors.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill will also provide powers for the Minister to appoint food security officers from among SFA officers or officers of any other Singapore public sector agency.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These appointed officers will be vested with monitoring and investigating powers, which are detailed in Part 13 of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill also empowers SFA to appoint "outsourced enforcement officers" to supplement its resources in carrying out selected functions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The scope of powers conferred to outsourced enforcement officers will be much more limited, as they are not public service officers.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: All outsourced enforcement officers, authorised officers, food inspectors and food security officers, will be issued identification cards that they must carry at all times when exercising their powers conferred under the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Egregious cases involving fatalities or intentional contamination of food, will be referred to the Police for investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon will elaborate on these measures in his speech.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Before I conclude, even as this Bill updates our food safety regime and strengthens our food security, many of the requirements will not be new to businesses and are already implemented today.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: By simplifying and bringing about consistency, the Bill reduces regulatory complexity for businesses, which in turn reduces compliance costs.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The food security requirements which Senior Minister of State Koh will elaborate on shortly, will also help increase businesses’ resilience and ensure operational continuity.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As we have consolidated all food related functions under a single agency, SFA, there is a need to do the same with our legislation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Grace, you wanted the Senior Minister of State to continue?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Yes, I would like Senior Minister of State Koh to continue with his speech, as I had alluded to earlier.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before that, Minister Grace, do you want to put the question?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will further elaborate on four areas: first, how the Bill will enable a shared commitment across Government, industry and consumers in pursuit of food safety; second, how we aim to minimise regulatory burden on the food industry; third, how we intend to strengthen our food resilience in the face of emerging challenges; and fourth, how the Bill will be implemented in stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The agri-food supply chain is getting increasingly complex, involving multiple stakeholders and more potential points of failure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Before food reaches our tables, the base ingredients are very likely grown in multiple countries, processed in yet another country, and then packaged and distributed to supermarkets and retail food businesses located locally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ensuring food safety from farm to fork requires every player across the food value chain to play their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It requires a shared commitment from Government, industry and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Parts 3 and 11 of the Bill regulate the import and the production of animal feed for food-producing animals, and Part 11 regulates the use of plant pesticides that are for growing food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Contaminated feed can expose food-producing animals to food-borne illnesses which can endanger consumer health and disrupt farm production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Excessive use of plant pesticides can leave high levels of harmful chemical residues on fresh produce, which may be difficult to wash off and pose health risks to consumers when ingested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The changes better match and support the respective regulatory missions of SFA and NParks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA’s concern is one of food safety and security for humans, whereas NParks considers protection of animal health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, under the Bill, businesses which manufacture animal feed for food producing animals will need to get a licence from SFA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Businesses which manufacture animal feed for non-food producing animals will need a licence from NParks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will ensure that feeds used are fit for their intended purposes and makes it clearer for our businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Currently, plant pesticides for both food and non-food plants require registration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Going forward under the Bill, product registration will only be mandatory for pesticides used on edible plants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Given that such plants would be ultimately consumed by people, improper use of pesticides can pose food safety risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Pesticides use for non-food plants will no longer require registration as they are not intended for human consumption and will not compromise food safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Existing registrations of food plant pesticides will be transitioned without the need for re-registration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Certification will continue to be required for all pesticide operators applying or supervising pesticide use on edible plants that are intended for human consumption, to ensure that these individuals are trained to apply pesticides safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This excludes the use of pesticides on edible plants grown for personal consumption, such as those in home gardens, or whole edible plants which are retailed in pots, such as potted herbs and ornamental plants like kumquats, which though can be eaten, largely serve more for ornamental purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Water is another key component, integral to every stage of the food value chain from production to preparation for sale or supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under Part 6 of the Bill, we will continue to require those providing a drinking water service to supply wholesome drinking water that is safe for human consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As technology advances, we are seeing innovations across different parts of the food value chain, along with the emergence of innovative food types.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Their long-term effect on human health needs to be evaluated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We must therefore indicate clearly to businesses which are developing or selling these products what their responsibilities are.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This category will comprise yet-to-be approved novel foods, genetically modified, or GM, foods, and insect-like species.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Once approved, such food will then be taken off the defined food list and may then be freely supplied in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Bill formalises SFA’s existing practice for novel foods, insects and GM foods, and seeks to ensure any food safety risks are identified early, without stifling innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Over time, this would foster greater trust and confidence among consumers and industry stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We do not expect the Bill to lengthen the approval process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA will continue to engage with food companies and provide guidance to facilitate the approval process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Alongside safety regulations, marketing plays a crucial role in communicating crucial information about food such as ingredients, allergens and nutritional value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Modern marketing strategies have also transformed how businesses influence consumers’ food purchase decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, Part 10 of the Bill sets out offences relating to misleading or deceptive marketing, covering newer forms of advertising and innovations in food labelling such as the use of QR codes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It also more clearly defines the parties responsible for ensuring accurate and substantiated food labelling and advertising.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It can be hard for consumers to verify the credibility of claims such as the composition, effect and origin of food before consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Misinformation can potentially compromise food safety and consumer health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Provisions under the Bill will place the onus on food suppliers to provide accurate information and representations of the food so that consumers can make accurate, informed choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Therefore, food-borne illnesses can be reduced significantly when food workers understand the importance and the basics of food handling and safe practices; and are subject to monitoring of their food handling proficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A food business licensee should be proactive in ensuring that food workers are current in their food safety knowledge and attend refresher training before their training certifications expire.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These measures will help to foster a strong food safety culture, reinforce food safety protocols, reduce the risk of safety lapses and ultimately protect consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Businesses can use SFA’s newly launched Food Handler Digital Data Hub to track the expiry dates of their workers’ certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The food industry is responsible for ensuring that their food is safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is not practical nor possible for SFA to verify and test all food items before consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We take a risk-based approach, aligned with international standards, to inspecting the safety of our food at the border, prioritising checks on food items that have higher safety risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, food products may sometimes still be found to be unsafe for consumption after they enter the market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When this happens, the food industry and SFA must be able to swiftly recall products to prevent the products from further circulating in the market and to reduce the potential for widespread illness or harm from occurring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To implement swift recalls of products, there must be proper record-keeping.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While some progressive industry players practice record-keeping, it is not consistently implemented across the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a result, significant effort is often required to trace implicated food batches during incidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To address this, Parts 3, 4 and 11 of the Bill imposes traceability and record-keeping obligations on selected licensed food businesses, licensed importers and licensed animal feed producers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA will then identify other affected companies to ensure coordinated and timely responses to protect consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Effective traceability allowed for the swift identification and recall of the affected mooncakes, as the business had a good record-keeping system in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The business was able to isolate the contaminated mooncakes and recall them swiftly with precision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This minimised the cost impact for the business as well because the alternative would have been to recall every single batch of mooncakes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To support the industry in this transition, SFA will undertake consultations in detailing records to be kept in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA will provide guidance documents to help compliance with the regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA is also developing a portal to facilitate the submission of documents from those required to maintain traceability records.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are calibrating and updating our regulations to align with SFA's risk-based approach to food safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Instead of prescribing requirements across businesses' different operating contexts, each business will have the flexibility to devise and implement preventive measures suited to their operation model to ensure safe food and animal feed that is fit-for-purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will be done through the Food Control Plan and the Feed Control Plan, which will be introduced as licence conditions under Part 4 and Part 11 of the Bill respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: All licensable food businesses which are not in primary production must design and implement a Food Control Plan, while licensed animal feed producers must design and implement a Feed Control Plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, businesses are already required to show they have measures to ensure food safety before SFA grants them a licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: By taking an outcome-based approach, the Food Control Plan would not prescribe specific measures, but allow businesses to consider what works for them to meet food safety outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This approach also recognises that food business licensees understand their operations best and are well-positioned to design effective food safety solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They will need to maintain these solutions to ensure hygienic and safe conditions and implement them throughout the entire licence period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It also ensures that food business licensees stay accountable even as new food products and business models emerge while encouraging innovative means to ensure food safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA will provide guidance on the scope of the Food Control Plan and the Feed Control Plan, according to the operating modality of the different businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: My Minister also, earlier, mentioned how some breaches, which are offences under existing law, will be decriminalised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under Parts 3, 4 and 11 of the Bill, SFA will decriminalise non-compliances such as breaches in licence or permit conditions that are less egregious in nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Proportionate regulatory actions, such as suspension of licence, imposing of financial penalties and issuance of directions, may be taken instead to avoid over-penalising less serious infringements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Minister mentioned earlier, Singapore is no stranger to food supply disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a small country which imports most of our food, we will not be able to insulate ourselves entirely from global food supply disruptions and the risks of unsafe food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Local production buffers against the impact of supply disruptions and add to Singapore's food security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For farms to viably produce and scale up in the long term, we must balance sustainability with productivity to ensure that farming activities do not harm the environment in which the animals and the plants need to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Farmers will need to come up with their methods and processes addressing the key areas of waste, feed, fish stocking, biosecurity and disease management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Sea-based aquaculture farmers will also have to state how they will monitor water and sediment quality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: All licensed farmers will need to appoint trained personnel to oversee implementation of the FMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Two farming enterprises that have already benefited from having comprehensive farm management and documentation systems are Metropolitan Fishery Group, a local fish farm; and Sustenir Agriculture, a local vegetable farm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Both farms are certified under Singapore's Good Agricultural Practices, a farm management standard that ensures food safety, produce quality and environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These practices have improved the farms’ operational efficiency, leading to higher productivity and safer, higher-quality produce for their customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The practices have also helped the farms to foster a culture of continuous improvement in farm management and production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, we are optimistic that similar requirements in the FMP will benefit other farms as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The FMP implementation will be phased in, to allow time for transition and SFA will provide the necessary support to help farms adjust to the new regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This includes working with Temasek Polytechnic's Aquaculture Innovation Centre to conduct training to guide farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The training course will be subsidised for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA will also provide guidance documents to help farmers understand the requirements and implementation of the FMP and work with relevant agencies to contextualise requirements for different farm types.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA also rolled out the Aquatic Animal Health Service in August 2023 to provide aquaculture farms with funded veterinary consultations, to assist them in farm management, disease diagnoses, prevention and control.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: More recently, in November 2024, SFA had announced the updated Singapore Aquaculture Plan and initiatives that seek to uplift the aquaculture sector to be one that is more productive and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the fragility of global food supply chains, as unexpected, unprecedented lockdowns disrupted production and logistics, causing delays and shortages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Geopolitical tensions, more recently, and climate change also continue to add pressure to food systems worldwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a small country with limited natural resources, import diversification remains a key strategy alongside efforts to build up our local production as a buffer against supply chain shocks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, in the face of severe food supply disruptions or emergencies, these measures alone may not be enough.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Any food supply disruption could have significant impacts on businesses, consumers and the Singapore economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But it is hard to predict when a significant food disruption might occur.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On the other hand, food importers and wholesalers have limited incentives to hold reserve stocks above the commercial stockholding level and to invest in back-up food storage and distribution facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In the absence of Government intervention, Singapore may not keep sufficient domestic food stocks or back-up arrangements to mitigate the impact in food supply disruption scenarios adequately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The MSR would help to ensure that we have a certain level of in-country stocks to tide over impacts to supply during potential disruptions in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, SFA only administers a Rice Stockpile Scheme, requiring rice importers to stockpile rice as an import licence condition under the Ministry of Trade and Industry's Price Control Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Instead of a licence condition, the MSR is a legal obligation under the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Minister will appoint a Director-General for Food Security, or DG (FS), to administer Part 2 of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The role of the DG (FS) will be to oversee and coordinate the formulation and implementation of our food security strategies in a comprehensive and effective manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Part 2 of the Bill will enable the Minister to declare other essential food items or agri-food production inputs to be subject to stockpiling requirements if the need arises in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That said, there are currently no plans to extend the stockholding requirement to entities other than rice importers or to other commodities beyond rice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will consult closely with the industry before prescribing any other food or agri-food production input as an MSR product and any activity as an MSR activity attracting the stockholding requirement and provide sufficient lead time for the industry to meet the new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For rice importers, the shift in legislative regime to the MSR will not change what they basically need to do today, which is to continue to stockpile prescribed quantities of rice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under clause 23, a stockpiling obligation arises for an entity, called an MSR entity, when the entity is given a formal written notice, called a "Trigger Notice", from the DG (FS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The trigger notice will indicate the specific requirements, such as minimum stockholding quantity, the daily and average monthly minimum, the storage location, the duration of the obligation and the implementation timelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Every MSR entity will need to maintain a minimum daily MSR product stock and a minimum average MSR product stock over a prescribed period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Part 2 of the Bill will also confer powers on the DG (FS) to collect data and information from participants in the agri-food supply chain, other than the ultimate consumer and others closely connected to the agri-food supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is to allow the DG (FS) to monitor and assess ways to strengthen Singapore's food resilience in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This information will also be used to support the administration of the MSR scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Steps will be taken to ensure only what is necessary is collected and that what is collected is kept confidential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, the DG (FS) will specify the data required, how and when it should be provided and for what purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, the DG (FS) will also work closely with relevant industry stakeholders to build up data reporting capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This includes, reviewing data collection processes and encouraging the adoption of technological solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, the DG (FS) will take the appropriate data protection measures to ensure the data will not be mishandled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Information will not be disclosed to persons outside of the Singapore Public Sector except in an anonymised form or as required by an order of Court.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will implement changes in phases to facilitate a smooth transition for the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The industry and public will be informed ahead of the implementation of the relevant provisions to allow time for them to prepare for the changes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It will enable MOH to issue, administer and enforce food-related regulations for the purposes of promoting better health for the general public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Food choices impact on nutrition and our health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Unhealthy diets increase our risk of developing chronic diseases, such as hypertension, diabetes, heart disease and cancer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Regulatory measures for health promotion purposes pertaining to food complement voluntary and educational efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH currently taps on SOFA and its subsidiary legislation, the Food Regulations, to make such regulations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Examples include, Nutri-Grade labelling and advertising prohibitions for beverages that are higher in sugar and saturated fat; and the ban on trans-fat, also known as partially hydrogenated oils (PHOs) in food.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The intention is for SOFA to be repealed and replaced by FSSB.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While the primary purpose of FSSB is for food safety and security, it would be appropriate for FSSB to also support better population health and nutrition, given the close link between food, health and nutrition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This will allow MOH to continue with our current health promotion measures that are in place under SOFA and to implement additional measures, if needed, to improve population health in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, such regulations are administered and enforced by MOH but made with powers vested with the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment under SOFA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: FSSB will allow for clearer delineation of Ministerial responsibilities between the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment and the Minister for Health, while allowing MSE and MOH to regulate the food supply chain for our respective purposes under a common regulatory regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Key provisions in the FSSB for better health and nutrition are consolidated under Part 9.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The first category is more stringent regulations that apply only to "target food".

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include regulations to prohibit import of a food; prohibit or restrict the way a food is manufactured, supplied or used in the manufacture or preparation of other foods; prohibit or restrict the way the public acquire or access a food; and require warnings to be included in food advertisements or food labels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: An example of an existing regulation that falls in this category is the ban on PHOs, which currently prohibits the import of any edible fat or oil that contains PHO for use as an ingredient in other foods and the use of edible fat or oil that contains PHO in the manufacture of other foods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The PHO ban aims to reduce the population's consumption of artificial trans-fat which is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To continue with the PHO ban under the FSSB, the Minister for Health will need to determine that cardiovascular disease is an NCD of public health interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This may be done in consultation with the Director-General of Health and the public will be notified of this determination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: PHO will be identified as a target food as it contributes to the occurrence of an NCD of public health interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: More stringent regulations that continue the current PHO ban may then be made as subsidiary legislation under the FSSB.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The other category of regulations can apply to all foods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include regulations to restrict import of a food, prohibit or restrict content used in advertisements or labels of a food, require display of prescribed dietary and nutritional information about the food at food premises and prohibit or restrict the medium or way in which food is advertised, sponsored or promoted for sale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: An example of an existing regulation in this category is the prohibition of claims on the advertisements or labels of infant formulas that idealise its use or compares it to breast milk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH intends for the existing food regulations for health promotion purposes to continue under the FSSB.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Should there be any new regulations, MOH and the Health Promotion Board will appropriately consult the public and industry to ensure that measures are practicable and implementable, as per our current practice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For regulations to be effective and meet their policy intent, they need to be enforced appropriately.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support the enforcement of any Part 9 regulation, the FSSB will empower the Director-General of Health to appoint enforcement officers, who are referred to as Part 9 enforcement officers in the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The investigating powers provided to such enforcement officers are outlined in Part 13 of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Non-compliance with the remedial notice without a reasonable excuse will be an offence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The main intent is to limit the impact of a contravention on the general public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Enforcement officers will issue a remedial notice if it is appropriate to give the person an opportunity to remedy the contravention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Otherwise, MOH may prosecute a person for the contravention of a Part 9 Regulation without first giving a remedial notice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I support this Bill, which allows Singaporeans to put food on the table with peace of mind every day and addresses the existential issue of food security for our nation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Last year, my fellow Members, Ms Poh Li San, Ms Hany Soh and Mr Edward Chia and I tabled the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Good Samaritan Food Donation Act and the Food Safety and Security Act are complementary pieces of legislation, which strike a balance in ensuring safety of food while reducing food waste and insecurity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification to raise on this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the supply of food past its labelled date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By labelled date, I am referring to expiry dates, consume-by dates, use-by dates, sell-by dates and best-before dates.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, it is already an offence to sell food that is past its labelled date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This includes donating or giving food without receiving any money or money's worth.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some groups rescue and redistribute food that is past its labelled date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is in the spirit of saving food that may be edible past its labelled date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some groups, such as SG Food Rescue and Divert for 2nd Life, educate consumers to use the look-smell-taste test to determine if food past its labelled date is still safe to eat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, if a retailer has expired food and permits an individual to take them for their individual consumption, would the retailer be committing an offence?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If no supply of food past its labelled date is permitted at all, can Minister share how the Ministry intends to mitigate food wastage?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, will SFA consider encouraging retailers to look for alternative avenues to sell or supply food that is close to its labelled date?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will SFA provide more support for initiatives and companies that help to redistribute food that is close to its labelled date?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The MSR will require certain industry participants to hold a certain level of food or agri-food production input.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I agree with the requirement, which strengthens Singapore's food security.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But it may also increase the risk of food waste.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry share what measures will be taken to ensure that food waste is minimised if MSR is imposed?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, will the Ministry support stakeholders subject to the MSR in reselling, redistributing or donating stocked food that is approaching expiry?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Food waste can also occur if stakeholders do not have the logistical and operational capacity to properly maintain the stockpiles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry also confirm that the MSR quantity that will be set will take into account stakeholders' logistical and operational capacity to maintain the stocks?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Ministry also support the stakeholders that may be subject to the MSR in building their logistical and operational capacity?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final point is on the pre-market approval regime for defined foods.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Part 5 of the FSSB provides a new framework for pre-market approval of novel food technologies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Novel food technologies are an opportunity for Singapore to reduce our reliance on imported food and reduce our carbon footprint from importing food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 13(1) sets out three categories of "defined food".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are novel food, genetically modified food and insect-like species as food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In turn, "novel food" is defined to include a substance that "has not been used to a significant degree as food for a period of at least 20 years, whether within or outside Singapore".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is some subjectivity in determining whether something has been used to a significant degree as food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry provide more guidance on how it will consider if a food or production process has gained sufficient normalcy that it is no longer considered novel in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How will the public and industry be made aware that the "defined food" is now considered by the Ministry to be normal "food" in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will there be a plan for publicity and education?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, I would like to seek clarifications on several aspects to ensure that the legislation is both effective and considerate of residents' concerns.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It also mandates farm management plans for local farms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While these provisions aim to strengthen food security, I urge the Minister to address the potential financial burden on our local farms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will these measures lead to significant cost increases for farmers, potentially disincentivising local agricultural investments?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Singapore's 30 by 30 initiative, which aims for 30% local food production by 2030, is an ambitious and important goal.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, if compliance with MSR or farm management plans under clauses 21 to 24 increases operational costs substantially, we risk undermining the very farms we seek to support.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Minister elaborate on how the Government intends to alleviate these financial pressures?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For example, are there plans for subsidies, grants or technical support to help farmers comply without jeopardising their livelihoods?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, the prohibition on selling such imports raises enforcement challenges.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Given the sheer volume of personal imports and the rise of online transactions, does SFA have sufficient resources and intelligence capabilities to enforce this regulation?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Additionally, clause 160 prohibits selling personally imported food.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If individuals buy more than they can consume, what are their options?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Would they be penalised for reselling excess items, or would gifting or donating be permissible?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clarity on enforcement mechanisms is critical to prevent undue penalisation of well-meaning individuals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I would suggest that SFA collaborate with ecommerce platforms like Shopee and Carousell to monitor and regulate transactions effectively, while minimising inconvenience to residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clause 144 extends food safety regulations to donations, ensuring that all consumed food is safe.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, we must ensure this does not inadvertently discourage food donation efforts, especially those supported by community initiatives like our Yio Chu Kang food rescue programme.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Minister clarify how clause 144 interacts with this Act?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will volunteers and donors continue to be shielded from penalties for unintended oversights?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Without assurances, these efforts to reduce food waste and support the community may be impacted.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, I caution against applying penalties in ways that deter volunteerism or community-based food rescue.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Minister confirm whether exemptions or safeguards will be in place to protect well-intended individuals contributing to food security?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I commend this focus on public health, I question the necessity of separating these provisions from the SOFA.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Consolidating them under SOFA instead could streamline the regulatory framework and reduce complexity for businesses and consumers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Minister elaborate more on why the current approach was chosen and how this enhances clarity or efficiency?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, its success depends on addressing key concerns.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, we must ensure that the proposed MSR supports rather than hinders our local farmers' efforts toward the 30 by 30 goal.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, enforcement of personal food import allowances must be practical and clearly communicated to avoid unfair penalties.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, food donation initiatives should be encouraged, not discouraged, by ensuring sufficient legal protection for volunteers and donors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Additionally, consolidating regulations on public health under existing legislation like SOFA could simplify compliance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: More importantly, we must remain mindful of affordability for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As food costs rise, any new measures should prioritise accessibility to ensure no resident is left behind in our pursuit of safety and security.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I urge the Minister to address these points to ensure that it strengthens our food security, promotes public health and upholds the values of affordability and community solidarity.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Part 2 of the Bill is titled Strengthening Resilience of Food Supplies in Singapore.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I would thus like to focus on our food resilience and how we can build an environment that enables a thriving local agri-food ecosystem as a co-pillar of this.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: My speech today will cover two areas: one, resilience farming; and two, moving from support local to champion local.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Post pandemic, attempts have been made to diversify our import sources and we set a goal for local food production.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: SFA is overseeing these efforts, from the Lim Chu Kang Master Plan for the High Tech Agri Food sector to the Agri Food Cluster Transformation Fund and the Singapore Agri Food Enterprises Federation Limited to facilitate long-term commercial contracts between farmers and food businesses.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Our starting point should thus be the concept of resilience, especially in the context of food.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We are therefore far from being said to have food resilience.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This is clearly evident in the SFA strategy to diversify food import sources, encouraging consumers to support local and boost local food production.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: However, are our efforts tackling the sources of food sufficient to enable us to achieve food resilience?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: According to a 2020 paper on the resilience of local food systems and the links to food security published in the Food Security Journal, I quote: "Resilience is about the capacities of households and communities to deal with adverse events in a way that does not negatively their well-being and/or functioning." The framing of resilience in this context is therefore broader and more holistic than simply addressing food security.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It is understanding three dimensions: first, exposure, that is, how much of our communities are exposed to externalities or risks; second, sensitivity, how much harm would it cause; and third, adaptive capacity.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The ability of our communities to mitigate the harmful effects.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: For example, a pandemic is an exposure risk.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Our high dependence on a small handful of countries for a high proportion of food imports is a sensitivity factor and the financial ability of households is a measure of adaptive capacity.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: A holistic, resilient building frame entails the need to recognise the interplay between these three dimensions of exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Such an overarching frame for resilience will guide the top level objectives that we should be setting, for example, our thirty by thirty goal, and to foster the right holistic ecosystem to enable our agri food sector to thrive across the entire value chain.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This means from subsidising, financing, design and conceptualising the farms to the streamlining of multi-agency red tape, and local food affordability and access.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Expanding this frame would ensure we always think beyond diversifying import sources and local production.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: SFA's vision is safe food for all and its mission is to ensure and secure a supply of safe food.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: SFA's mandate is therefore centred around the themes of food safety and security.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If SFA is responsible for our 30 by 30 goal, we should thus refresh and add to this mandate to reflect a frame of resilience.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: An aligned mandate will enable SFA to effectively oversee the implementation of holistic policies that complement its role as an accountable body for Singapore's overall food resilience.
